File: https://wethepeople305.org/docs/organizer-criteria.md

# Organizer admission criteria

**DRAFT. Waiting for the founder's approval. Not in force until this line is removed.**

As of 2026-10-29.

## What the organizer role is
Anyone can have a citizen account. The organizer role is for organizations that do civic work in Miami-Dade. It will unlock organizer tools (watchlists, alerts, bulk access) as they are built. It is granted by these published criteria, checked by a person, not by name or by who someone knows. The same criteria apply to every organization, whatever its views or politics.

A person can hold both roles. An organizer is still a citizen.

## Criteria
An organization must meet all five. Each has an id, used by the application form and the API.

1. `miami-dade-civic-work`: The organization does civic work in Miami-Dade County: for example attending public meetings, public comment, voter education, or neighborhood service.
2. `verifiable-public-presence`: The organization can be checked in public: a website, a public social media page, a Florida corporation record, or a listing of its public meetings.
3. `not-a-campaign`: The organization is not a candidate, a campaign, a political party, or a political committee, and is not run by one.
4. `named-contact-for-review`: The organization has someone who can answer questions from the reviewer about this application.
5. `code-of-conduct`: The organization agrees to the project Code of Conduct and to use organizer tools within it.

## How to apply
1. Create an account at [/account](https://wethepeople305.org/account) (a passkey, or Google).
2. Fill in the form at [/organizers](https://wethepeople305.org/organizers): organization name, a website or public page, which criteria you meet, and a short statement (20 to 1,000 characters) on what you do in Miami-Dade.
3. Your account page shows the status: pending, approved or declined.

The API is `POST /api/v1/organizer-applications` with a session cookie. See `identity.md`.

## How review works
- An admin reviews each application against the five criteria, using public records: the website, the Florida Division of Corporations, the Florida campaign finance database, meeting minutes.
- The admin approves or declines and may add a short note. Approval grants the organizer role at once.
- An admin cannot review their own application.
- Admin is not a role anyone can apply for. It is granted only by the founder running a command (see `identity.md`).

## Open questions for the founder
- Should individuals (not organizations) be able to qualify, for example a neighborhood leader with a record of public comment?
- Should all five criteria be required, or some subset?
- How long should an approval last before it is checked again?
- Should a declined applicant be able to reapply at once, or after a wait? Today they can reapply at once.
- Who besides the founder reviews applications, and should the reviewer's name be public?

---
File: https://wethepeople305.org/docs/decisions/README.md

# Architecture decision records

Short records of choices that shape the platform. Each has a status, a date, the context, the decision and its consequences. To change a decision, add a new record that supersedes the old one.

- 0001-headless-first.md: every capability is an API operation and an MCP tool before it has a screen
- 0002-cost-ladder.md: route every operation to the cheapest tier that can do it
- 0003-do-now-by-rules-not-model.md: the do-now list comes from four fixed rules
- 0004-ballot305-source-adapter.md: Ballot305 is read through one adapter
- 0005-address-never-stored.md: an address is passed through and never stored
- 0006-money-figures-stay-on-ballot305.md: money is shown only with full context, on Ballot305
- 0007-mcp-and-openapi-from-one-schema.md: OpenAPI and MCP tools are generated from one schema
- 0008-ledger-moves-to-platform.md: the ledger API is served here from a copy of Ballot305's data; after Nov 3 Ballot305 reads it
- 0009-passkeys-native-google-federated.md: passkeys are the native sign-in; Google is an optional federation

---
File: https://wethepeople305.org/docs/decisions/0001-headless-first.md

# 0001. Headless first

- Status: Accepted
- Date: 2026-10-23

## Context
Residents and organizers work in many tools: browsers, chat assistants, Slack, spreadsheets. A platform built screen-first ends up with logic only the screen can reach, and every other client gets less.

## Decision
Every capability is an API operation and an MCP tool before it has a screen. The web pages are clients of the same API with no private path. Today that means `/api/v1/precinct` and `/api/v1/your-area`, the same two operations as MCP tools at `/mcp`, and `public/your-area.html` calling the API.

## Consequences
- An assistant connected over MCP can do what the page does.
- New features start with a schema, not a layout.
- The API must carry provenance and plain-language reasons, because a client may show only the data.
- Identity by key (OAuth) is planned; until then everything is public and read-only.

---
File: https://wethepeople305.org/docs/decisions/0002-cost-ladder.md

# 0002. Route every operation to the cheapest tier that can do it

- Status: Accepted
- Date: 2026-10-23

## Context
Model calls cost money and add error. A one-person nonprofit project cannot carry open-ended spend, and residents deserve answers that can be checked.

## Decision
Tiers, in order: 0 static files, 1 code and rules, 2 cache, 3 small model with a schema, 4 large model, 5 a person. A task starts at the lowest tier that can answer it. Tier 3 and 4 calls go through `lib/model.mjs`, which reads the routing table in `config/models.json`, validates JSON against a schema, retries once, then falls to the next model. Results are cached by prompt version and input hash.

## Consequences
- Public routes today use tiers 0 to 2 only.
- Every model task needs a schema and an eval file.
- Each call is logged with model, tier, cost and input hash, so cost per task is a query.
- Swapping providers is a config change checked by evals.
- Planned: per-key and per-worker spend caps, and a usage ledger in D1.

---
File: https://wethepeople305.org/docs/decisions/0003-do-now-by-rules-not-model.md

# 0003. The do-now list comes from fixed rules, not a model

- Status: Accepted
- Date: 2026-10-29

## Context
"What to do now" is the part a resident is most likely to act on. A model ranking could be wrong in ways nobody can see, and could tilt toward one side without anyone intending it.

## Decision
`lib/your-area.mjs` builds the list from four published rules, at most one action each: vote within 30 days of an election; weigh in on the weightiest posted item with its meeting still ahead; speak at the next regular meeting closest to home; reach the district office closest to home. Item weight is a fixed sum (place 8, money 4, lobbyist 4, hearing 2, prior action 1). The rules are returned in every response.

## Consequences
- Anyone can see why an action ranks where it does and reproduce it.
- The list is the same for every precinct with the same data, regardless of who is in office.
- The rules are blunt. Changing them is a code change with tests.
- A model may later suggest actions, but only as reviewed candidates, never in this list without a rule.

---
File: https://wethepeople305.org/docs/decisions/0004-ballot305-source-adapter.md

# 0004. Read Ballot305 through one source adapter

- Status: Accepted
- Date: 2026-10-29

## Context
The researched data (officials, calendars, ways to take part, posted items) lives in Ballot305 today and is served by its public API under CC BY 4.0. It will move into this platform after the election. The move should not touch feature code.

## Decision
`lib/sources/ballot305.mjs` is the only code that reads Ballot305. It exposes `now`, `upcoming` and `precinctCodes`, takes an injected `fetch`, and carries the license and attribution. The Worker passes a fetch that caches upstream reads at the edge for 15 minutes.

## Consequences
- Swapping the source later means changing one file.
- Every response names the source, license and methodology.
- Ballot305 outages and errors reach residents as a 502, softened by the 15 minute cache.
- Ballot305 stays a separate site; this platform never writes to it.

---
File: https://wethepeople305.org/docs/decisions/0005-address-never-stored.md

# 0005. An address is passed through and never stored

- Status: Accepted
- Date: 2026-10-29

## Context
A home address is the most sensitive thing a resident gives the platform. Kept anywhere, it could be joined to what they look up and when.

## Decision
`/api/v1/precinct` sends the address to the Esri geocoder, then the U.S. Census geocoder if needed, and sends only coordinates to the Miami-Dade precinct layer. The address is not logged, stored or cached; the response is `Cache-Control: no-store`. The event shape in `lib/events.mjs` has no address field and rejects props named like address, email, name, phone, ballot, street or ip. The page keeps only the precinct code, in the link and in the browser's own localStorage.

## Consequences
- A precinct code is the most specific location the platform keeps.
- The geocoder providers still see the address. This is disclosed in the privacy notice.
- Features that need the address again (a nearest polling site, for example) must ask for it again or work from the precinct.

---
File: https://wethepeople305.org/docs/decisions/0006-money-figures-stay-on-ballot305.md

# 0006. Money figures stay on Ballot305

- Status: Accepted
- Date: 2026-10-29

## Context
A dollar figure next to an official's name reads as an accusation unless it comes with what it is out of, where it came from and how it was counted. Ballot305 shows money with its full context, denominator and methodology. A short card here would strip that.

## Decision
Your area and the API do not include money behind officials. They link to Ballot305 for it. Amounts on posted agenda items (what an item spends) are shown as stated in the record.

## Consequences
- No figure on this platform is shown without its denominator.
- Residents take one extra click to see money.
- If money moves here later, it moves with the same context and methodology, not as a bare number.

---
File: https://wethepeople305.org/docs/decisions/0007-mcp-and-openapi-from-one-schema.md

# 0007. MCP tools and OpenAPI come from one schema

- Status: Accepted
- Date: 2026-10-29

## Context
An API document, an MCP tool list and the handlers written by hand drift apart. An assistant then calls a tool that no longer matches the API, or validation differs between the two.

## Decision
`lib/api-schema.mjs` defines each public operation once: id, method, path, parameters with JSON Schema, response schema, errors, and whether it sends personal data. From it:
- `openApi()` builds the OpenAPI 3.1 document at `/api/v1/openapi.json`.
- `mcpTools()` builds the MCP tool list served by `lib/mcp.mjs` at `/mcp` (stateless Streamable HTTP, JSON responses). Tools are marked read-only.
- `checkParams()` validates input for both HTTP and MCP calls.
The Worker runs one handler per operation id for both.

## Consequences
- A new operation is added in one place, then given a handler.
- HTTP and MCP return the same data with the same validation.
- Contract tests check the generated outputs against the schema.
- The UI's types are not generated yet (planned).

---
File: https://wethepeople305.org/docs/decisions/0008-ledger-moves-to-platform.md

# 0008. The ledger moves to the platform

- Status: Accepted
- Date: 2026-10-29

## Context
The ledger (officials, official actions, roll calls, gifts tied to actions, calendars, posted agendas, procurement, payments, connections, contacts) is built and served by Ballot305 today, at `ballot305.org/api/v1`, from JSON committed in its repo. Architecture section 4 makes the ledger a platform service and section 11 step 3 moves Ballot305's `src/api.js` here. The founder wants the platform to own the data now. The election is Nov 3, 2026, so Ballot305 must not change before then.

## Decision
Phase 1 (now): copy and serve.
- `scripts/sync-ballot305-data.mjs` copies the files the API reads from a Ballot305 checkout into `public/ledger-data/` and records the Ballot305 commit and copy time in `SOURCE.json`. It is idempotent and refuses a file over the 25 MiB static asset limit. The workflow `sync-ledger-data.yml` runs it hourly and on demand, and commits only when data changed. It does not deploy.
- The data is served as static assets because the Worker reads it through the ASSETS binding, the same way Ballot305 does, and so the raw files that `/bulk` lists resolve here. `decisions.json` (28 MB) is not copied; its split (one index plus one file per body) is, as on Ballot305.
- `lib/ledger/` is `src/api.js` ported as plain JavaScript with the data passed in. HTTP is split out: the Worker routes, sets headers and loads the data once per isolate.
- The operations are in `lib/api-schema.mjs`, so they appear in OpenAPI and as MCP tools (`ledger_*`; bulk is HTTP only). Paths and bodies match Ballot305's. A parity test runs Ballot305's own `api.js` and the ledger over the same files and requires identical bodies.

Phase 2 (after Nov 3): Ballot305 becomes a client (section 10). It reads the ledger from this platform's API, with no shape changes. Then either the copy job reverses direction (Ballot305's pipelines write, the platform is the source of truth) or the pipelines move here behind the records service (section 11 step 4).

## Consequences
- The platform serves ledger data without calling Ballot305 at request time. `your_area` still reads Ballot305 through its adapter (0004) until phase 2.
- The copy lags Ballot305 by up to an hour plus the next deploy. Brit deploys; the sync job never does.
- The ledger API returns tie amounts and money summaries, as Ballot305's API does. Decision 0006 still governs screens and `your_area`: no bare figure. The API keeps every caveat field (`match`, `basis`, `timing`, `days`, `actionSplit`, summary denominators), and the docs ask clients to repeat them with any amount.
- The isolate holds the whole index in memory (about 60 MB built in Node, under the 128 MB isolate limit). A cold isolate spends a few hundred milliseconds building it. When the data outgrows that, it moves to D1 (section 11 step 6).
- Data stays CC BY 4.0 with attribution to Ballot305.

---
File: https://wethepeople305.org/docs/decisions/0009-passkeys-native-google-federated.md

# 0009. Passkeys are the native sign-in; Google is an optional federation

- Status: Accepted
- Date: 2026-10-29

## Context
The platform needs accounts: citizens, organizers admitted by criteria, and later Ballot305 signing in through the same service. The founder's rules: people create an account on wethepeople305.org itself, Google is never the only way in, and we collect the minimum.

The usual native option, an emailed magic link, needs a service that sends email. Cloudflare Email Routing receives mail but cannot send it, so magic links would need a paid sender and would make an email address required. Passwords need storage, reset flows and breach handling, and they get phished.

## Decision
- Native sign-in is a passkey (WebAuthn). The server stores only the public key. No email, no password, no outside service. Server side uses `@simplewebauthn/server` 14.0.3, which runs on Cloudflare Workers without `nodejs_compat` (Web Crypto only; tested in workerd). The browser side is the browser's own WebAuthn API in a small file we serve, so no CDN and no CSP change.
- Google OpenID Connect is offered beside it: code flow with PKCE, state and nonce, server-side exchange, ID token verified against Google's keys. We ask for `openid` only, plus `email` when the person ticks a box.
- Sessions are opaque random ids in a `__Host-` cookie, hashed at rest, 30 days rolling, revocable. No JWTs in the browser.
- Storage is D1 behind a Store interface with an in-memory adapter (architecture section 3).
- The admin role is granted only by a command the founder runs, never by a route.

## Consequences
- Anyone with a current phone or computer can make an account without giving any personal detail.
- A person who loses every device with their passkey, and has not linked Google, loses the account. Synced passkeys (iCloud Keychain, Google Password Manager, 1Password) make this rare. Account recovery is not built; adding a second passkey or linking Google is the advice today.
- We cannot email people unless they give an address. That fits the minimum-data rule.
- The architecture's planned email magic-link adapter is not built. Apple sign-in can be added later as another federation behind the same linking rules.
- API keys for the organizer tier are a separate, later step; this record covers people signing in.

---
File: https://wethepeople305.org/docs/privacy.md

# Privacy

This describes the site as of 2026-10-29.

## Looking up your precinct
When you enter an address, the site sends it to:
- the Esri World Geocoder, and if that does not find it, the U.S. Census geocoder, to get coordinates;
- Miami-Dade County's precinct map (GIS), which receives only the coordinates.

Those services have their own privacy terms. The site does not log, store or cache your address. The answer is sent with `Cache-Control: no-store`.

## What stays in your browser
After a lookup, the page puts your precinct code in the page link (for example `/your-area?precinct=033.0`) and saves it in your browser's localStorage under the key `wtp.precinct`, so the page opens to your area next time. It stays on your device. Clear it by clearing site data in your browser.

## What the site records
The site records events about how it runs: which route was called, how long it took, whether it worked, and for Your area, the precinct code. Events have no field for an address, name, email, phone or IP, and the code refuses to record one.

## Hosting
The site runs on Cloudflare. Like any host, Cloudflare receives standard request data such as IP address, browser and the page requested. The site does not add logging of that data. To stop the address lookup being used for bulk geocoding, Cloudflare counts lookups per IP address for one minute; the count is held by Cloudflare's rate limiter, not stored or logged by the site. Cloudflare's own processing is governed by its privacy policy.

Pages load fonts from Google Fonts, which receives the standard request data for those files.

## Accounts (optional)
You do not need an account to use the site. If you make one (at /account), we keep only:
- an account id we make up, the date it was created, and your roles (citizen; organizer if an application is approved);
- for each passkey, its public key, a counter and when it was last used. The private key stays on your device;
- if you link Google, Google's account number for you (not your name or photo). Your Google email only if you tick the box to save it;
- anything optional you add: a display name, an email address, a precinct code;
- if you apply to be an organizer, what you put in the application;
- a hash of your session id, so you stay signed in for up to 30 days.

We do not store your name, address, phone number or IP address with your account. Sign-in events record only which route ran and whether it worked. Details: `identity.md`.

### Deleting your account
Sign in at /account and choose "Delete my account", or send `DELETE /api/v1/me` with your session. It removes your account, passkeys, Google link, sessions and organizer applications at once, and cannot be undone. Your device may still keep the passkey; you can remove it in your password manager. To unlink Google on Google's side, use your Google account's "Third-party connections" page.

## Cookies
The site sets cookies only when you sign in:
- `__Host-wtp305_session`: keeps you signed in. HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax. Deleted when you sign out.
- `__Host-wtp305_oauth`: holds a one-time value for up to 10 minutes while you sign in with Google.

No other cookies. No analytics or advertising cookies.

## What the site does not do
- No ads, no tracking pixels, no selling or sharing data.
- No email from us unless you give an address, and then only about your account or an application.
- No model sees your address.

## Officials
The site shows officials' public office contacts as published by their offices. It does not show home addresses or personal contacts.

## Contact
privacy@wethepeople305.org
